verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents an org-level service connection for Sprites: connect a service once, every Sprite can reach it, nobody pastes a token, access can be scoped down to a single endpoint, and credential rotation propagates automatically. That directly addresses avoiding hand-wired credentials, but it is limited to the Sprites product and described only in marketing-level copy. For regular apps, the evidence shows only Secrets and Managed Postgres, and one user reports Postgres failing to link to their app when following the guide. Missing for 10: documented native bindings for databases and storage in code, detail on which services and APIs are supported, coverage beyond Sprites, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect my code to external services like databases, APIs, and storage through native bindings with minimal boilerplate instead of hand-wiring SDKs and credentials

citations.quote: Connect a service once for your whole org, and every Sprite can reach it. Nobody pastes a token.
Grant access on purpose: by Sprite name, by label, or down to a single endpoint
Rotate once and every Sprite has the new credential.
